entries.title: A great name, little to show
entries.literal_meaning: The name is big; the appearance is small.
entries.explanation: The dictionary takes this beyond appearance: a famous name can belong to someone inadequate in practice. The balanced halves puncture an imposing reputation. Our application asks what stands behind an impressive introduction, without making physical size a measure of ability.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନର ଟୀକା ଏହାକୁ ଦେଖାଶୁଣାଠାରୁ ଆଗକୁ ନିଏ: ବଡ଼ ନାମ ଥାଇ ମଧ୍ୟ କାମରେ ଅଯୋଗ୍ୟତା ଥାଇପାରେ। ଦୁଇ ଖଣ୍ଡର ବିପରୀତତା ଖ୍ୟାତିର ଆଡ଼ମ୍ବରକୁ ଫୁଟାଇ ଦିଏ। ଆମ ପ୍ରୟୋଗରେ ଚମତ୍କାର ପରିଚୟ ପଛରେ କି କାମ ଅଛି, ସେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଉଠେ; ଶରୀରର ଆକାର ଯୋଗ୍ୟତାର ମାପ ହୁଏନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: The source contrasts a large reputation with inadequate performance.
entries.odia_summary: ବଡ଼ ଖ୍ୟାତି ସହ କାମର ଅଯୋଗ୍ୟତାର ବିରୋଧ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଏକ ପଢ଼ାଚକ୍ରରେ ବହୁ ପ୍ରଚାରିତ ପୁସ୍ତକର ଉଦାହରଣଗୁଡ଼ିକ ଭୁଲ ବୋଲି ଦେଖାଗଲା। ଜଣେ କହିଲେ, “ନାମ ଶୁଣି ଭରସା କରିଥିଲି; ଏବେ ଭିତରର କାମକୁ ଦେଖିବା।” ଅନ୍ୟଜଣ ଏହି ଢଗଟି ମନେ ପକାଇଲେ। / A reading group finds errors in a heavily promoted book. One reader says, “I trusted the name; now let us examine the work.” Another recalls this saying. The book discussion is invented.
entries.cultural_context: The following dictionary note supplies the practical-capability reading. No named person, incident, first author or customary performance setting is identified.

entries.title: A headache without a head
entries.literal_meaning: There is no head, yet it has a headache.
entries.explanation: The line removes the head and keeps its ache: an impossible complaint compressed into a joke. The entry separately gives a figurative sense of deep anxiety. Our reading transfers the paradox to worry about a responsibility that does not exist; the source supplies no particular occasion for that use. It does not establish that anyone’s actual pain is false.
entries.meaning_odia: ମୁଣ୍ଡକୁ ବାଦ ଦେଇ ତାହାର ବଥାକୁ ରଖାଯାଇଛି—ଅସମ୍ଭବ ଅଭିଯୋଗଟି ହିଁ ପରିହାସ। ଏହି ଶବ୍ଦର ଅଲଗା ଲକ୍ଷଣାର୍ଥରେ ଗଭୀର ଚିନ୍ତା ଦିଆଯାଇଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ନଥିବା ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ନେଇ ଚିନ୍ତାକୁ ଏହି ବିରୋଧାଭାସରେ ଦେଖାଯାଏ; ସେ ପ୍ରୟୋଗର କୌଣସି ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ଅବସର ଉତ୍ସ ଦିଏନାହିଁ। କାହାର ପ୍ରକୃତ ଯନ୍ତ୍ରଣା ମିଛ ବୋଲି ଏଥିରୁ ପ୍ରମାଣ ହୁଏନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: An impossible headache becomes our analogy for a worry without its supposed responsibility.
entries.odia_summary: ଅସମ୍ଭବ ମୁଣ୍ଡବଥାରେ ନଥିବା ଦାୟିତ୍ୱର ଚିନ୍ତାକୁ ନେଇ ଆମର ପରିହାସ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଅରୁଣ ଏପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ଗଢ଼ା ହୋଇନଥିବା ସମିତିର ବୈଠକ କେଉଁଠି ହେବ ବୋଲି ଚିନ୍ତା କରୁଥିଲେ। ସାଙ୍ଗ କହିଲେ, “ଆଗେ ସମିତି ହେଉ, ତାପରେ ଜାଗା ଖୋଜିବା,” ଓ ଢଗଟି ମନେ ପକାଇଲେ। / Arun worries about a meeting venue for a committee that has not been formed. A friend says, “Let the committee exist first; then we can find a room,” and recalls the line. This exchange is invented.
entries.cultural_context: The bodily impossibility is preserved. The anxiety definition is lexical context, not a supplied gloss of this quotation; the modern committee application is editorial and gives no medical advice.

entries.title: A fitting pair
entries.literal_meaning: Whatever suits each: soak black gram and rice.
entries.explanation: The entry defines the opening as what is appropriate to a person or thing. Its answer brings black gram and rice together in the action of soaking. Our reading follows the pairing: usefulness can depend on what accompanies something. The quotation names no finished dish, proportion or rule for sorting people into groups.
entries.meaning_odia: ଆରମ୍ଭର କଥାକୁ ଅଭିଧାନ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତି ବା ବସ୍ତୁ ପ୍ରତି ଯାହା ଉପଯୁକ୍ତ ବୋଲି ବୁଝାଏ। ଉତ୍ତରରେ ବିରି ଓ ଚାଉଳ ତିନ୍ତେଇବାର କାମ ଆସେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ମେଳଟି ମୁଖ୍ୟ—ଗୋଟିଏ ଜିନିଷ ସହ କଣ ରହୁଛି, ତାହା ତାର ଉପଯୋଗକୁ ବଦଳାଇପାରେ। ଢଗଟି କୌଣସି ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତ ଖାଦ୍ୟର ନାମ, ପରିମାଣ ବା ମଣିଷକୁ ଗୋଷ୍ଠୀରେ ବାଣ୍ଟିବାର ନିୟମ ଦିଏନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: A food pairing carries our reading about useful accompaniment.
entries.odia_summary: ଖାଦ୍ୟର ମେଳରେ ଉପଯୋଗୀ ସଙ୍ଗତିକୁ ନେଇ ଆମ ପଢ଼ା।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଏକ ଶିଶୁପାଠରେ ମାନଚିତ୍ରଟି ଏକା ଦେଖି ପିଲାମାନେ ବୁଝିପାରୁନଥିଲେ। ଶିକ୍ଷକ ଛୋଟ ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନାଟି ପାଖରେ ରଖି କହିଲେ, “ଏବେ ଦୁଇଟିକୁ ମିଶାଇ ପଢ଼ିବା,” ଓ ଢଗଟି ମନେ ପକାଇଲେ। / Children find a map unclear on its own. A teacher places a short description beside it: “Now read the two together,” recalling the saying. This classroom use is invented.
entries.cultural_context: The food image and explicit appropriateness gloss are retained. Complementary teaching materials are our application, not a documented traditional use or a recipe.
